title: Scan a patient's wristband: roll the limp forearm over to bring its barcode out, and hold it there while you scan
instruction: Scan the barcode on the training arm's wristband with the handheld scanner. Then put the scanner down on the table and lay the arm back palm down.
context: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00: 'Administer medications to patients...'; about 3.2M US jobs) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061.00; 0.65M) scan the patient's wristband before every medication, and phlebotomists (31-9097.00; 0.14M) before every draw: it is how the two-identifier rule (Joint Commission NPSG.01.01.01) is met at the bedside. Bands turn on the wrist, so the code is often underneath. A limp forearm rolls back when let go, so one hand must turn it and keep holding while the other aims a triggered scanner inside its reading range, field of view and tilt limits, within its 9.9 s decode session. Unlike RoboTwin 2.0 scan_object (a box and a scanner are both picked up and brought together) or TK-UJVHAJ (cartons turned toward a fixed scanner), the code is on a person: it cannot be carried or let go, and the limb must be handled gently, never dropped.
setup: Metres; x forward, y left; heights above the table top; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305). Layout A (layout B, BAND_LOT=B, in brackets). (1) Arm board, fixed: vinyl-covered foam block 90 x 261 x 75 mm high, centred at (0.440, -0.301) [(0.455, -0.316)]. (2) Training arm: the right forearm and hand of an adult training arm, silicone skin over a rigid core, 1.2 kg, 455 mm from elbow end to fingertips: forearm 60 mm across and 215 mm long, wrist 54 mm across, hand 80 mm wide, 22 mm thick at the palm and 18 mm at the straight fingers, thumb along the palm's edge. It lies along +y, palm down, thumb toward the robot, its axis 108 mm above the table and 3 mm clear of the board; elbow end at (0.440, -0.435) [(0.455, -0.450)], fingertips at y +0.020 [+0.005]; the hand and wrist overhang the board's end. Its elbow end turns in a steel bearing block (70 x 56 mm, 148 mm tall, fixed; real build from catalogue parts, with a drawing and a torque check, in README 'Building the arm fixture') about the forearm's long axis: 0 deg palm down (a stop), 90 deg thumb up with the palm toward the robot, up to 170 deg. A torsion spring at the pivot returns it palm down: 0.035 N m/rad, so 0.055 N m holds a quarter turn (1.4 N at the hand's edge); damping 0.003 N m s/rad. Let go, it rolls back. (3) Wristband: adult thermal wristband, polypropylene, 25.4 mm wide, 0.3 mm thick, blue, fastened snug round the wrist with its centre 245 mm from the elbow end, clasp on the back of the wrist. Its white label panel is on the palm side, with one Data Matrix (ECC 200, 22 x 22 modules of 10 mil, 5.6 mm square) centred under the wrist: palm down, the symbol faces the board 6 mm above it. (4) Scanner, free: cordless pistol-grip imager, Zebra DS2278-HC (17.5 x 6.6 x 9.0 cm, 214 g, white and blue ABS), awake, handheld trigger mode (Standard/Level), paired to a host. It lies on its left side, reading toward +x, head toward +y: the foot's underside on the handle's axis at (0.270, -0.400) [(0.255, -0.385)], the handle's middle 33 mm above the table, the scan window at x 0.320 [0.305]. Trigger: a 14 x 25 mm blade on the handle's front, 5 mm travel, 2.5 N at full travel; its switch closes at 3 mm. Good-decode light on the back of the head. Friction (static/dynamic): skin 0.9/0.8, scanner 0.7/0.6, board 0.6/0.5. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at the ready pose with the grippers open.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step from the forearm's angle, the trigger's travel and the poses of the scanner and grippers. READ (the scanner's published figures): a trigger pull (3 mm or more) opens a decode session of at most 9.9 s; the scanner reads once the symbol's centre and four corners have all been, for 0.25 s without a break, 0.8 to 15.7 cm from the scan window, inside the imager's 32.8 x 24.8 deg field of view, on a surface tilted no more than 65 deg from facing the window, in clear line of sight (the board, the training hand and both grippers block it), and moving under 13 cm/s across the scanner's view; its light then turns green. A timed-out session reads nothing until the trigger is released and pulled again. TOO FAST: the forearm turning faster than 200 deg/s at any step (let go from a quarter turn it rolls back at up to 380 deg/s; the demo stays under 53). SHOWN: the forearm at 60 deg or more for 1 s. PUT BACK: the scanner lying on the table (lowest point within 5 mm of it, under 0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s), the forearm within 10 deg of palm down and turning under 10 deg/s, and each gripper's grasp point 30 mm or more from both. Score at the end of the run: 1.0 read, never too fast, all put back; 0.75 read and never too fast, but not all put back; 0.5 read, but too fast at some time (the arm dropped or jerked); 0.25 no read, but shown and never too fast; otherwise 0. Success = 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial: the scanner decides the read (its beep and green flash, and the record its host logs); the forearm's speed is judged from video filmed end-on against a protractor dial at 60 frames/s or more (too fast: more than 10 deg between two frames 50 ms apart, the same 50 ms average the simulator checks), its final angle with a protractor or level on the back of the hand, the release from a photo.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at step 468 (23.4 s)
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the scanner back on its tape marks, on its left side, and check that it is awake. The forearm returns palm down by itself; check that the band has not slipped (symbol centred under the wrist). In simulation, reset restores all poses and clears the scanner's session and the read.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The arm is rigid (no soft skin, wrist or finger joints); a limp forearm's roll-back is a torsion spring. The band is fixed to the wrist. The scanner is boxes with a sprung trigger; no light or image is simulated: a read is task code applying the DS2278's published range, field of view, tilt and motion figures, a line-of-sight check and its 9.9 s decode session, plus 0.25 s of steady view (our figure). Print contrast and glare are not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper hovered over the scanner and then over the arm's wrist without picking the scanner up or turning the forearm; the left arm stayed back); demo: 1.0 (read at step 223, success at step 468)
